bull.b: Fourteen consecutive quarters of positive same-shop sales, alongside nine quarters of customer-visit growth, indicates repeat demand is broadening rather than relying only on new stores. This supports revenue resilience and gives the existing base a durable platform for future expansion.

Management's pipeline supports at least 185 openings in 2026 and about 250 in 2027, while recent shops annualize near $2 million and the 2025 class delivers roughly 45% year-two cash-on-cash returns. Strong unit economics can make expansion self-reinforcing.

Revenue reached $1.88 billion TTM and net income $92 million, while operating cash flow rose to $366 million and free cash flow turned positive at $95 million. The earnings turnaround and improving cash generation strengthen funding capacity for continued store development.

bear.b: Debt of $1.21 billion versus $798 million of equity produces 1.27x debt-to-equity. Although leverage improved from prior years, this debt burden can restrict financial flexibility and increase sensitivity to softer traffic, margins, or cash generation during expansion.

Coffee, occupancy, utilities and freight costs are pressuring economics: occupancy and other costs reached 18.0% of company-operated revenue, while Q4 beverage, food and packaging costs are guided to 27.5%. Persistent input pressure could limit margin expansion.

Management expects 2027 growth mainly in existing states and acknowledges that denser development causes sales transfer or cannibalization. Even with site underwriting, this can reduce incremental store productivity and make the large opening pipeline less additive to company-wide growth.
